title: Bias–Variance Tradeoff — Noise Sets a Floor

body:
## Noise Sets a Floor

Even a perfect weather model cannot know a sensor error or truly random gust. Some prediction error cannot be removed from the available inputs.

Expected error can be thought of as squared bias, variance, and irreducible noise. The pieces explain why reducing one source may expose another.

Bagging lowers variance by averaging unstable models. Boosting often lowers bias by adding corrections, though both can behave differently with noisy data.
common_mistakes: Choosing a remedy without comparing training and validation behavior.
Assuming model size alone determines effective complexity.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Noise Sets a Floor” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: The tradeoff explains underfitting, overfitting, and why model complexity needs validation.
